## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block in which nine people hold nine things by saying a number out loud twice at the fourth hour and one man who cannot cross safely without somebody standing with him is not in the middle of it, and the Gatehouse falls anyway, and it is not in this county and is not shown.** It is also the block that prints the antagonist's name for the second and last time in the volume, in a document, and spends the last of the volume's six names, and it is the block whose resolution is a refusal and a practice rather than a road saved by a man walking up it.

`outline/volume-16.md` §8 Block 5 and §9 and §10 are binding and are not softened by anything in this file. `outline/series.md`'s Volume 16 row is fixed. `outline/ending.md` is fixed. **DO NOT MOVE THE ENDING. DO NOT INTRODUCE A NEW FINAL ENEMY. THE ANTAGONIST IS EDRIC HUNN AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS VOLUME PUTS HIM IN A ROOM.**

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE VOLUME'S CLIMAX IS NOT A ROAD AND IT IS NOT A BATTLE AND IT IS NOT SEEN.** `outline/volume-16.md` §9: nine people hold nine things by saying a number out loud twice at the fourth hour, and one man who cannot cross safely without a custodian is not in the middle of it, and the Gatehouse falls anyway. **THE GATEHOUSE IS TAKEN IN THIS BLOCK BY PEOPLE WITH A CROWN'S WARRANT AND ABOUT NINE HUNDRED YARDS OF A STAIR, AND NOBODY IN THIS COUNTY SEES IT HAPPEN, AND NO CHAPTER ENTERS IT, AND THE MECHANISM IS NOT EXPLAINED AND NO CHAPTER SAYS WHAT A ROADMARK IS.** `outline/volume-16.md` §1 is binding: it is not a volume in which the mass cull is defeated in this county, and it is not a volume in which a path community is rescued, exhibited, or explained.

**THE SECOND AND LAST PRINTING OF THE ANTAGONIST'S NAME, ONCE, IN A DOCUMENT, AT THE FOOT OF SOMETHING WITH A HAND ON IT, AND NEVER IN A MOUTH.** `outline/volume-16.md` §16 item 4 caps it at two for the whole volume and Batch 0004 has spent one at `chapter-0781.md`. **Print it exactly once in this block, in a document, and nowhere else and never in a mouth. `Hunn` on its own is not a printing and the bare surname may not stand as a printing either. A document carrying it is a roll, a covering paper, a letter, a notice, an endorsement, a covering sheet, a warrant, a second copy or an endorsement on a roll, and a chapter may not have a character read it aloud as a document, because a name read aloud in a room is a name printed in a mouth. The protagonist may see it, may not ask about it, and nobody asks him anything.** A natural carrier already on the page is **the second copy of the roll and the folded sheet inside its covering paper**, or a covering paper over a third copy, or the endorsement on the office copy that comes back to the boards. **The rolled-up thing must come off the same ordinary post and must be nailed up by a man in a coat with a Crown's button on it who does not know what it is carrying.**

**THE NAME BUDGET FOR THIS BLOCK IS EXACTLY ONE AND IT IS THE LAST OF THE VOLUME'S SIX.** `Renn Ottery`, `Pell Arkwright`, `Wyn Fell`, `Abel Chinn`, `Brida Lenth`, `Aren Kest`, `Mara Vey`, `Orme Skell`, `Dav Rundle`, `Tarr Lyster` and `Corve Sallow` are returns and cost nothing. **THREE OF THE VOLUME'S SIX ARE ALREADY SPENT AND THE SIXTH SPENT WAS `Brida Lenth` AT `chapter-0782.md`, so after this block spends one there is none left, and the volume closes with seven of its chapters' worth of people still described by their trades.** `Sabra Rolf` and `Gallow` may not be used for a new first name, and neither may `Iven` and `Marrow`, and neither may `Renn` or `Ost` as a surname, and neither may any first name or surname already printed in the hundred files from Chapter 701 onward. **A SUCCESSOR TO THIS BLOCK IS THE PHASE THAT WRITES THE VOLUME-CLOSE RECORD AND IT MAY NOT SPEND A NAME, AND THIS BLOCK MAY NOT LEAVE THE BUDGET UNSPENT BY ACCIDENT.**

**AREN KEST IS NOT THE CUSTODIAN OF ANY OF IT, AND THE VOLUME SAYS SO IN FRONT OF ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED PEOPLE ON A MARKET MORNING, AND NOBODY ARGUES AND NOBODY IS THANKS.** `outline/volume-16.md` §10 item 5 is the resolution and it is not a defeat and it is not an honour. **He says that out loud, at a table where about four hundred people are standing, and about nine of them stop, and about four hundred go on, and that is the beat and it may not be softened into a speech about how much it cost him and it may not be made into a confession.** The practice has to survive him for eleven days inside this block, which means at least eleven datelines or eleven named mornings on which two other people said the number and he was not one of the two.

**THE TWO PEOPLE CHOOSE A SHARED HOUSEHOLD AND DEFER THE LEGAL FORM, AND NEITHER OF THEM MAKES THE RELATIONSHIP THE SOURCE OF THE PLAN.** `outline/series.md`'s Volume 16 Resolution line and `outline/volume-16.md` §10 item 4. **THE WORD IS NOT PRINTED, NOTHING GOES IN ANY DOCUMENT, THE FOUR AND A HALF YEARS ARE NEVER DESCRIBED AS FOUR AND A HALF YEARS ABOUT THE TWO OF THEM, AND NOBODY IS THANKED AND NOBODY COMMENTS.** The legal form stays deferred to Volume 18. **And it may not be a declaration scene: the house's mechanism for this is a third person working inside the two of them as though the arrangement were already a fact of the work, and `chapter-0782.md`, `chapter-0783.md` and `chapter-0785.md` have spent the copyist, the word keeper and the lamp that was not put out, so a successor may spend a fourth of those and may not spend the same one twice in a way a reader would notice.** **No chapter may end on the two of them standing nine feet apart, because `chapter-0780.md` has already spent that beat.**

**THE RESOLUTION IS WHAT `outline/volume-16.md` §10 GIVES AND IT IS SIX THINGS AND NONE OF THEM IS A RESCUE.** A mass cull announced and not defeated in this county, and what is defeated is the assumption that a county which cannot call a meeting cannot refuse a roll. A closed path not destroyed, its silence a political loss, and no power available to anybody in this volume repairing it. The Gatehouse occupied and not shown and not in this county, the main world facing a constitutional collapse, and this county's contribution to the Charter being a refusal and a practice. Two people choosing a shared household and deferring the legal form. Aren Kest not being the custodian of any of it. **And the volume ends on the twenty-fifth of Frostmonth YR 323, which is six days before Hearthmonth, exactly as Volume 15 ended six days before Hearthmonth YR 322, and the volume is the third running to end on the twenty-fifth of a month and the first to end on a Wednesday, and the last line of the volume is a room and a floor and a lamp and a road that somebody else is holding.**

**THE COST OF THE BLOCK IS ON THE PAGE AND IS NOT CURED IN IT, AND IT IS NOT THE COST OF THE PREVIOUS BLOCK AGAIN.** The leg, which now takes eleven miles in four hours before light and about nine otherwise and which is worse than it was at the start of this volume; the ear on the side the stick is on, **which Batch 0004 stated as a fact he plans around and which this volume states as permanent**; the standing fact that he cannot be near the works without somebody standing with him; **and, per `outline/volume-16.md` §9, a path bleed that does not fully fade and the last clear thing he will ever have of his mother, neither of which is in any earlier page of this volume and both of which must be on this one, plainly, without a panel and without an explanation.** **The scar is three hundred and ninety days old at the block's last dateline and is not cured and is not going to close over, and the ninth yard of the wall has not been started and does not start, and the mallet is not picked up, and the ninth thing is still shut by nine hurdles by the people at the end of it who would like them to stay.**

## 5. The ending of the block

**A completed beat.** The Gatehouse falls and is not shown. The practice has been said by other people for eleven days and has survived him. **The roll on the boards is not filled in and is not destroyed and its nine lines are empty on it and on its copies, and the folded sheet inside the covering paper is still there in an unclaimed hand, and nobody in nine counties has said who wrote it.** The four lines of chalk are under a hood where the rain does not reach and are still not writing, or they are still four and the page says so. The leaf at the back of the day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody and is not the record, **and the register holds ten questions and this volume closes with no finding under any of them, and no fifth head is ruled.** The ninth thing is alive, unnamed, unheld and shut, and the volume ends on that and not on a cure.

**`outline/volume-16.md` §11's three hand-offs are CARRIED FORWARD OUT OF THIS VOLUME AND NONE OF THEM IS CONDUCTED HERE:** a refusal in writing that is also a refusal to govern, a sealed route that somebody has claimed can be made to speak, and an occupation with a gate on it and a keeper who is a local, which `chapter-0790.md` set up with a badge-man of about fifty-eight who wrote nothing and a counter and a door at the low end of that market street with a man behind it who was born in that street. **A successor in Volume 17 inherits all three in this volume's terms and may not learn the opposite of them.**

**`state/continuity.md` 1722 and `state/open-threads.md` 719 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it: four lines on a sill are not the beginning of a cure and a page in a woman's hand is not a cure either, a closed path is not destroyed and that is not good news, and being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour and nobody was told so and nobody wrote it down.**

## 6. The prohibitions, in one list

**This list is additions to `state/open-threads.md` items 711 to 726 and 727 to 735, and to 705, 704, 703, 702, 700, 699, 698, 697, 694 and 690, and to every clause of 686, 684, 680, 679 and 674 that is still true. It does not replace them.**

- **Do not print a System panel.** The volume's one was spent at `chapter-0776.md` and is seventeen words and this block prints none. **And this block prints the volume's only panel-shaped paragraph about a bleed, and it is not a panel and it is not bold and it is not alone and it is not spoken aloud and nobody else heard it.**
- **Do not print the antagonist's name more than once, or anywhere except a document, or in a mouth, and do not print it a third time anywhere in the project.**
- **Do not conduct any of the three hand-offs.** No hurdle is lifted and no bar is tried up that shut track, because the roadkeeper who claimed a bar will get up it also said in the same sentence that he is not going to be the one who tries it, and **a successor may not make him the one who tries it in this block either.** No third trip up the cart track and nobody shown standing behind all nine hurdles. **The occupation with a gate on it is not entered and the keeper who is a local is not asked what a gate is for.**
- **Do not open a route, do not lift the nine hurdles, do not close a route, and do not cut anything.** §12 gave Batch 0003 *a transfer witnessed and not conducted* and it has been had.
- **Do not explain the mechanism. Do not say what a roadmark is. Do not look at the notebook's separate leaf that says *a person*.** No character notices the warmth of the left palm, and no chapter of this block asks him about the transfer offered at `chapter-0670.md`.
- **Do not look over the ninth of the nine stones, do not cross them, do not show what is on the far side of them, and do not treat the omission as an oversight.** The dead grass in the scar stops at the ninth of them.
- **Do not reopen either refusal of Volume 15, do not argue with either, do not soften either, do not ask either of the two men who gave them anything, and do not put the man of forty-one in a scene or ask him anything.** He says sixteen words in Batch 0003 and is asked nothing before or after, and **he is not in a scene in Batch 0004 either, and he may not be in one here.**
- **Do not turn the nine houses at Wethergill into a body, do not turn the nine households at the mill lane into a body, and do not turn the nine who refused the roll on the first of Mudmonth into a body.** They are nine houses, nine households that voted, and nine people who said one thing each, and that is all.
- **Do not ask any of the nine who refused the roll for an account of having said it, do not ask the roadkeeper or the woman of about fifty-one about the broom straw, and do not ask anybody whether she wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**
- **Do not let the three answers to the roll become one answer, do not resolve the incompatibility between them, and do not let the protagonist be the author, the announcer, the summariser or the fourth voice of any of them.**
- **Do not fill the roll, do not have any person put a name against a road, do not have any road shut on the strength of the roll, and do not have the roll destroyed.**
- **Do not put the practice into the register, the day-book, or under a fifth head, and do not have the copyist rule a head.** The day-book stands at eleven entries and the fourth ruled head is empty and no fifth head is ruled and the leaf at the back carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody and is not the record.
- **Do not mend the separation by a declaration, do not print the word, do not put anything about the two of them in any document, and do not let anybody else comment on it, and do not let the relationship be the source of the plan.**
- **Do not fill or rule any head, put a finding under any of the ten questions, turn or time the half leaf, lift or schedule the bar at the Low Gate, lay or schedule the fourth course of stone, or pick the mallet up.** The ninth yard of the wall has not been started and does not start in this block.
- **Do not lift the cloth off the bench and do not have anybody ask what is under it.**
- **Do not cure the scar, do not say it is small, do not say it is going to close over, and do not start the ninth yard.**
- **Do not send anybody to the city four hundred miles off, do not reopen the shut road four hundred miles off, do not get the road that went quiet in Thawmonth YR 319 back, do not find the carter's mate, and do not trace who asked the fen county road office for the roll and do not trace who wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**
- **Do not merge the three series, derive one from another, change the band figure, or put a number in the drawer. Do not convert a path's count into main-world days, and do not month, weekday or tide a path mouth.**
- **Do not call any of the four holes in the arrangement small, do not resolve any of them, do not renumber them and do not open a fifth without saying on the page why four was not enough.**
- **Do not thank anybody, in any chapter, in any speech, or in any state file this block writes.**
- **Do not print the kin-term, and do not print *stage*, *ledger*, *qualification*, *failed*, *charter*, *custodian*, *mechanism*, *small*, *volume* or *block*.** The word *failed* is not used about the shut road four hundred miles off and is not used about anything at all in this volume.
- **Do not produce, mention or know about Ilyra Kest's route notes, and do not enter the Gatehouse.**
- **Do not introduce a new final enemy. Do not write a marker of any kind.**
- **THE NAME BUDGET FOR THIS BLOCK IS EXACTLY ONE OF THE ONE THAT REMAINS, AND NOT ZERO AND NOT TWO.**

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0790, 0787, 0782, 0783 and 0788.** Read them before writing a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else.

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names the figures in the chapter that are not in it. **THE CEILING IS 343 PENCE AND IT IS ARITHMETIC**, with the barred six **14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41** excluded. **The barred numerals may not be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere.** Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum.
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL SEVEN HUNDRED AND NINETY PRIOR FILES, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK EMPTY.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, the two-hundred and three-hundred band as well as the one-hundred band, plus the digit form, run over every file whole. **OVER SEVEN HUNDRED AND NINETY FILES THE USABLE FREE SET IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS ZERO, twelve values remain free, being 212, 218, 230, 254, 266, 273, 281, 308, 314, 321, 326 and 329, and every one of them fails the barred-over-figure filter on 20, 26, 38, 14, 26, 33, 41, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41, and the route below sixty is shut.** **THIS BLOCK'S TEN TOTALS WILL THEREFORE BE REUSES, AND THE HONEST THING TO DO IS WHAT ALL TEN OF BATCH 0004'S CLOSING PARAGRAPHS DO: NAME THE REUSE ON THE PAGE AND GIVE THE REASON, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC, AND A SUCCESSOR MAY NOT ADD ONE WORD MORE OF THAT REGISTER THAN *searched whole*, *barred numeral*, *route below sixty* and *file in the manuscript*, once each, and may not cut the column out.** Lifting the ceiling is an outline decision and not a writer's. **Batch 0004's totals, which a successor inherits as a record and not as its own, are 91, 104, 127, 147, 176, 199, 221, 247, 283 and 306 pence.**
4. **`about` density.** Batch 0004 runs **22.85 to 26.71** per 1,000 and no page is at or above 27.00, and its per-file column is 23.07 / 22.85 / 24.82 / 24.80 / 26.63 / 26.71 / 26.65 / 23.58 / 26.26 / 24.02. Batch 0003 runs 21.45 to 26.45 and Batch 0002 runs 21.45 to 26.41. **Aim for 22 to 27 and no page at or above 27.00. Keep the census sentence for the two or three beats in a chapter where who understood is the point and write the rest as action, weather, distance and silence. Do not write below 3,000 words and do not let a chapter run past about 4,300.**
5. **THE CENSUS INSTRUMENT IS NAMED AT `state/continuity.md` 1708 AND A WRITER WHO QUOTES A FIGURE MUST NAME IT WITH IT.** Split the ten files on the blank line and count every non-empty paragraph. **Basis A is every paragraph except the title line. Basis B is Basis A less FOUR named groups in this block, because this block prints no System panel: the ten datelines, the dialogue paragraphs, the bold cost codas and the bold closing money columns. A writer who quotes a Basis B figure must say in words which groups were taken out.** The opener test is every paragraph beginning `No`, `Not`, `Never`, `None`, `Neither`, `Nobody`, `Nothing` or `No one`. Batch 0004 is 0.0 and 0.0 and Batch 0003 is 0.0 and 0.0. **THE SEVENTY-FIVE PER CENT CEILING IS NOT CROSSED IN THE LAST THREE BLOCKS AND MUST NOT BE CROSSED IN THIS ONE.**
6. **Every count attached to a printed speech is footed off the printed words beside it**, and where a claim cannot be counted off the words printed next to it the claim is cut rather than left wrong. **A printed speech that has a word count beside it must have its words printed, and an unprinted speech must have no count.** This is the single most repeated finding in this manuscript's reviews. **The last block's four speeches footed at thirty-one, forty-two, sixteen and forty-five and the three answers to the roll may not be given a second time here, so any count in this block is a new speech and it is footed by counting the words on the page and not by remembering them.**

## 8. The running figures this block must keep

**Derive every one of these from the day number and never from a row, and print the figure at the chapter's OWN dateline. `state/open-threads.md` item 721 is the finding that eight of Batch 0003's ten drove paragraphs carried a wrong calendar date because the chain was derived once and handed on, three of them printing a day of a sixty-day month that cannot exist, and Batch 0004 carried it forward by deriving on each page. THE CHEAPEST CHECK IS THAT MUOMONTH IS SIXTY DAYS AND EVERY OTHER MONTH IS THIRTY, SO ANY DAY OF MONTH ABOVE THIRTY PRINTED INSIDE MUOMONTH IS WRONG ON SIGHT, and this block is entirely outside Mudmonth.**

- **The drove** goes up that lane on Thursdays and the count since the second of Mudmonth is floor((day - 2348) / 7) + 1 taken ON OR BEFORE the dateline. **It is 79 at day 2898, the last dateline of Batch 0004, and 89 at day 2970.** The drove paragraph's calendar date is the last Thursday on or before the dateline, being Embermonth the ninth, the twenty-third, the thirtieth, Wolfmonth the seventh, the fourteenth, the twenty-first, the twenty-eighth, Frostmonth the fifth, the twelfth and the nineteenth for the ten datelines in §3, and **a writer derives that date from the weekday and not from the count.**
- **The stone** has been carried two miles in one man's own hands since day 2347, elapsed and not inclusive. **It is 552 at day 2899 and 623 at day 2970.**
- **The scar** is counted from day 2580. **It is 319 at day 2899 and 390 at day 2970, and it is not cured and it is not going to close over.**
- **The ninth thing**, being the Wethergill end of a cart track, went quiet on the thirteenth of Hearthmonth YR 322, being day 2628, and nobody has been up that track since the second of Goatmonth, being day 2647. **Those two silence figures are counted from two different days and mixing them is the single most likely arithmetic defect in a chapter about that place: the last lime cart was 271 days ago at day 2899 and 342 at day 2970, and the road has been shut 252 days at day 2899 and 323 at day 2970.** Nobody goes up it in this block.
- **The practice mornings** are every day from 2611 to the dateline that is not a Thursday and not a Saturday. **The calendar count is 207 at day 2899 and 258 at day 2970, the count of mornings the practice was due on is 201 and 252, and the loss is six on every one of them and the six are the six of the seven practice mornings of the nine days of water in Mudmonth, and a successor inherits those six as gone and does not recover them.**
- **The number** said out loud at the fourth hour is **four**, it was eight until nine days of water, and it has not gone back, and two of the ten things came back after the water and two have not.
- **The printed notice** was read at the boards on day 2665, the first of Mudmonth was day 2706, it passed with nothing enforced and about nine people saying no in nine trades, **and it is a hundred and ninety-three days past its date at day 2899 and two hundred and sixty-four at day 2970 and has shut nothing.** Every reference to the instrument is *the Marshal's hand*, *that notice*, *the roll* or, in the one or two documents that carry the name in this block, the document itself.
- **The two refusals** of Volume 15 are days 2509 and 2521, and neither man is asked anything.
- **The brood** stands at five frames under about nine straw skirts and no sixth has gone in, and the young man of about nineteen has said out loud twice that he is not going to make more bees than the bees he has got. **Nothing is on the page about the skirts that a character has to act on.**
- **The standing broom** is about nine hundred yards of a line nine feet wide and the water laid nearly all of it flat, and it will not close over.
- **The wall's gap** is about nine feet long and four feet high and the ninth yard has not been started, and the mallet is on the bank two miles off with the line of stone and is not picked up. **Four separate things in this county are about nine feet across, being this gap, the width of the made road, the width of the standing broom and the distance of the man of thirty-two from the foot of the thirteen stairs. Carry the noun with the number every time and never print the number on its own.**
- **The four lines of chalk** are on the stone sill of that weigh-house door **under the hood where the rain does not reach**, they mean four, nobody has read them out loud, and the stick of chalk is in a press drawer and the man of about fifty-four has not asked for it.
- **The leaf at the back of that day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody**, and the day-book stands at eleven entries and the register holds ten questions with no finding under any of them. **The volume closes on both of those standing exactly where they stood, and that is the resolution and it is not a failure to have fixed them.**
- **The practice does not run on the market mornings**, because the room over the weigh-house is open on them.
